metadata.name: hook_rules
metadata.description: hookpool template: launch rules fixed at launch (sniper fee, creator fee, holder rewards, burn, buy limit, creator lock)

instructions.name: before_add_liquidity
docs: No liquidity is added while the sniper fee runs. The sniper fee is a pool fee: it
goes to every LP share. Without this, a wallet could add liquidity in the launch
slot and take most of a sniper's fee out again with it. Removing is never refused:
this hook has no callback for it.

instructions.name: claim_creator
docs: Pay `creator_owed` to the quote token account the creator names.

accounts.name: creator_quote
docs: Where the fee goes. Any token account of the quote mint the creator names.

instructions.name: claim_holder
docs: Pay a holder what it is owed, in the quote token, to the token account it names.

accounts.name: owner_quote
docs: Where the rewards go. Any token account of the quote mint the holder names.

instructions.name: claim_rewards
docs: Pay the staker's rewards, in the quote token, to the token account it names.

accounts.name: staker_quote
docs: Where the rewards go. Any token account of the quote mint the staker names.

instructions.name: close_holder
docs: Close a holder record that holds nothing and get its rent back: no coins, nothing
owed, nothing locked, and no early coins still under their lock.

instructions.name: execute
docs: Token-2022 calls this on every transfer of a strict coin, after the balances
moved. It refuses the transfer when a rule says so, and keeps the holder records
of both wallets equal to what they hold.
It takes effect only in the middle of a real transfer of this coin: both token
accounts must carry Token-2022's "transferring" flag, which only the token program
sets, for the length of its call into the hook. It makes no CPI.

accounts.name: authority
docs: owns the token account, whoever signs.

instructions.name: init_manifest
docs: One-time: publish the manifest and the extra-accounts list. Upgrade authority only.

instructions.name: init_pool_config
docs: By the launcher, before `create_pool`. Writes the rules, once, and creates the
treasury, the burn account and the stake vault. The pool's `hook_quote_treasury`
must be `cfg.treasury`.

accounts.name: hook_authority
docs: no data. The pool's `hook_swap` can spend only from accounts of this PDA, which is
why the two vaults do NOT belong to it: they belong to the config.

accounts.name: treasury_quote
docs: `init_if_needed`: anyone can create an associated token account for any owner, and
a plain `init` would let a stranger block this instruction by creating one of these
two first. An account that is already there is the same account: its owner is the
authority, and the mint and the owner are checked.

instructions.name: init_strict_config
docs: By the launcher of a strict coin, before `create_pool`, in place of
`init_pool_config`. The coin must be a Token-2022 mint whose transfer hook is this
program and can never be changed. The mint signs: only whoever creates the coin can
bind it to its rules, and only once. Writes the rules, creates the treasury, and
creates the account list Token-2022 passes to `execute` on every transfer.
A strict coin has every rate of a plain coin, the burn included. Its burn runs
through `run_burn_strict`. It has no burn account, no stake vault and no lock vault.

accounts.name: base_mint
docs: The coin. It signs, so only whoever creates the mint can bind it to its rules.

accounts.name: treasury_quote
docs: `init_if_needed` for the reason given at `InitPoolConfig`.

instructions.name: lock_creator
docs: Move coins from the creator's wallet to the lock vault, or move the date later.
The date never moves earlier, is never before the launch plus the lock declared
in the config, is always in the future and at most MAX_LOCK_SECONDS ahead.
`amount == u64::MAX` (`LOCK_WHOLE_BALANCE`) locks everything `creator_base` holds
when the instruction runs. A launch uses it for "what the first buy bought": the
client then does not have to know that amount to the unit before the transaction
lands.

accounts.name: lock_vault
docs: Owned by the config. Created by the first lock.

accounts.name: creator_base
docs: The coins to lock. The token program checks that `creator` may spend it.

instructions.name: lock_creator_strict
docs: The creator lock of a strict coin. The coins stay in the creator's own wallet and
the transfer hook refuses every transfer that would leave it with less than the
locked amount before `unlock_at`. (A vault, as on a plain coin, is impossible here:
this program would have to move the coin, and the token program would call this
program's own `execute` from inside that instruction.) The creator needs a holder
record. The rules of `lock_creator` hold: more coins or a later date, never an
earlier one; `amount == u64::MAX` locks everything the wallet holds.

accounts.name: creator_base
docs: in the handler.

instructions.name: open_holder
docs: A wallet asks for its share of the holders' rate on a strict coin. Signed and paid
by the wallet itself. From here on its balance counts. Opening twice does nothing.
It can be opened before the pool exists.

accounts.name: owner
docs: The wallet. It signs and pays: nobody registers somebody else.

accounts.name: owner_base
docs: Its address is checked in the handler.

instructions.name: run_burn
docs: Buy the coin from the pool with the burn pot and burn what was bought. Anyone may
call it, and whoever calls it chooses `min_amount_out`. So a run never buys at a
price or on a depth its caller just made (`burn_step` of the interface crate):
* it buys against an OBSERVATION of the pool that is at least BURN_INTERVAL_SLOTS
old. The first call of a pool only records one. A call that comes too soon fails
with `BurnTooSoon` and writes nothing.
* when the price is above the observed one by more than twice the cap, it buys
nothing and records the reserves as the new observation.
* otherwise it spends at most `burn_cap_bps` of the SMALLER of the quote reserve
now and the observed one, and records the reserves after the buy.
* between calls, every trade that starts below the observed price lowers the
observed price to the one it started at, without raising the observed depth
(`before_swap`, `burn_lowered`). So a price is bought at only when no trade
started below it for the whole interval.
Every call that returns Ok emits `BurnExecuted` with its outcome and sets return
data: the outcome byte, then quote spent and coins burned (`set_burn_result`).

accounts.name: platform
docs: The platform: its protocol fee and its hook fee cap decide how much a run may spend.

accounts.name: authority_base
docs: The burn account: the authority's ASSOCIATED token account of the coin and no
other, because everything in this account is burned. (The stake vault and the lock
vault belong to the config, not to this authority, so they could not pass here or
in the pool's `hook_swap` in any case.)

instructions.name: run_burn_strict
docs: `run_burn` for a strict coin: the same instruction in every respect but one. The
observation, the age it needs, the tolerance, the cap on the smaller depth, the
lowering in `before_swap`, the event and the return data are those of `run_burn`.
The one difference: the coins are bought through the pool's `hook_buy_burn`, which
burns them in the pool's vault. They are never transferred, so the token program
never calls `execute` of this program from inside this instruction, which the
runtime would refuse. A strict coin therefore has no burn account, and nothing a
stranger sends anywhere is burned with a run.

accounts.name: platform
docs: The platform: its protocol fee and its hook fee cap decide how much a run may spend.

accounts.name: base_mint
docs: Writable: the burn lowers the supply.

instructions.name: stake
docs: Move coins from the wallet to the stake vault. Restarts the unstake delay of the
whole record.

accounts.name: staker_base
docs: The coins to stake. The token program checks that `staker` may spend it.

instructions.name: sync_holder
docs: Anyone: lower a holder record to what the wallet really holds. A token Burn does
not call a transfer hook, so after a burn a record stands above the balance until
the wallet's next transfer, or until somebody sends this. It never raises a record.

accounts.name: owner_base
docs: in the handler.

instructions.name: unlock_creator
docs: From `unlock_at` on: move everything in the lock vault back to the creator and
zero the record.

accounts.name: lock_vault
docs: Owned by the config, which signs the transfer.

accounts.name: creator_base
docs: Where the coins go. Any token account of the coin the creator names.

instructions.name: unlock_creator_strict
docs: From `unlock_at` on: zero the creator lock of a strict coin. The coins were free
from that moment already; this clears the record.

instructions.name: unstake
docs: Move coins back to the wallet. Refused until UNSTAKE_DELAY_SLOTS after the
record's last stake.

accounts.name: stake_vault
docs: Owned by the config, which signs the transfer.

accounts.name: staker_base
docs: Where the coins go. Any token account of the coin the staker names.

types.name: BurnExecuted
docs: Emitted through event CPI by every `run_burn` that returns Ok. `outcome` says what it
did: `BURN_OBSERVED` (1, the first observation, nothing bought), `BURN_WAITED` (2, the
price was above the observation by more than the tolerance, nothing bought) or
`BURN_BOUGHT` (3). The observation is the one the call left in the config.

fields.name: amount
docs: Coins added by this call.

fields.name: locked
docs: Coins in the lock record after this call.

types.name: HolderRecord
docs: A wallet that holds a strict coin and asked for its share. PDA ["holder", pool, wallet].
The first six fields are the ones of a stake record, with the wallet's balance of the
coin where a stake record has the staked amount.

fields.name: balance
docs: What the wallet's associated token account held after its last transfer. The
holders' share is paid on this.

fields.name: acc_snapshot
docs: `acc_per_share` when this record was last brought up to date.

fields.name: owed
docs: Rewards settled into this record and not paid yet.

fields.name: early_bought
docs: Coins this wallet bought from the pool inside the early window. Until the unlock
its balance cannot go below this.

fields.name: locked
docs: The creator lock of a strict coin: the creator's balance cannot go below this ...

fields.name: locked_until
docs: ... before this unix time. Both zero for every other wallet.

types.name: LockRecord
docs: The creator lock of one pool. PDA ["lock", pool].

fields.name: amount
docs: Coins the creator put in the lock vault and has not taken back.

fields.name: unlock_at
docs: Unix time from which `unlock_creator` works. Zero when nothing is locked.

fields.name: curve_virtual_quote
docs: The curve launch (HOOKS.md section 2): the quote counted in the price of a new curve
pool without being there, and the real quote reserve at which it graduates. Copied
into each curve pool at creation; a later change does not touch running curves.
Either one at 0 switches curve launches off (`CurveDisabled`).

fields.name: curve_graduation_fee_bps
docs: Share of the target taken for the platform at graduation, at most
`HARD_MAX_GRADUATION_FEE_BPS`.

types.name: Rates
docs: The three shares of a trade, in basis points.

types.name: RulesArgs
docs: What the launcher chooses. The same fields, in the same order, as the rule part of
`RulesConfig`.

fields.name: treasury
docs: ATA of the authority PDA for the quote mint. Must be the pool's hook treasury.

fields.name: creator
docs: Who paid for this config. Must be the pool creator. Receives the creator fee.

fields.name: min_eligible
docs: Never zero once the pool exists, so it also tells whether the pool was created.

fields.name: fees_seen
docs: The pool's hook fees paid to the treasury, as of the last settlement.

fields.name: last_split
docs: The three rates of the last trade's side: what its fee is split by.

fields.name: obs_slot
docs: The observation `run_burn` buys against (`burn_step` of the interface crate): the
slot it was taken in and the pool's reserves then. No observation yet while a
reserve is zero. `before_swap` lowers the observed price, never raises the
observed depth, and leaves the slot, when a trade starts below the observed price
(`burn_lowered`).

fields.name: kind
docs: `KIND_PLAIN` or `KIND_STRICT`. Written by the instruction that creates the config.

fields.name: buy_mark
docs: 1 between `before_swap` of a buy and the transfer that pays that buy out. That
transfer, and any other transfer of the coin, sets it back to 0.

fields.name: vault_bump
docs: Bump of the pool's vault of the coin. Written by `on_pool_create`.

fields.name: max_wallet_amount
docs: The max wallet in units of the coin, from the supply when the pool was created.

types.name: StakeRecord
docs: One per staker and pool. PDA ["stake", pool, wallet].

fields.name: acc_snapshot
docs: `acc_per_share` when this record was last brought up to date.

fields.name: owed
docs: Rewards settled into this record and not paid yet.

fields.name: since_slot
docs: Slot of the last stake. `unstake` waits UNSTAKE_DELAY_SLOTS from here.

types.name: StrictArgs
docs: The rules of one pool and the running numbers. PDA ["cfg", pool]. This account is also
the owner of the stake vault and of the lock vault, and signs when coins leave them.
The three numbers of a strict coin, fixed at launch like the rest.

fields.name: max_wallet_bps
docs: Max wallet, in basis points of the supply. 0 = off.

fields.name: max_wallet_slots
docs: For how many slots after launch the max wallet holds.

fields.name: early_slots
docs: Buys from the pool in the first `early_slots` slots are "early". 0 = off.

fields.name: early_unlock_slots
docs: Early coins unlock at `start_slot + early_unlock_slots`.

fields.name: reserve_base
docs: Reserves at the moment of the callback (before the swap in `before_swap`,
after it in `after_swap`).
